'''Ravindra B. Bapat''' is an Indian mathematician known for the [[Bapat–Beg theorem]].

== Education ==
He obtained B.Sc. from [[University of Mumbai]], M.Stat. from the [[Indian Statistical Institute]], [[New Delhi]] and Ph.D. from the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] in 1981.<ref name="bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.isid.ac.in/~rbb/bioweb.pdf|title=Biography|publisher=Indian Statistical Institute, Delhi Centre|accessdate=15 April 2017}}</ref> His research interests include major contributions to matrix inequalities, [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrices]] in [[graph theory]], generalized inverses, and matrix analysis.

== Career ==
In addition to the numerous research papers in the reputed journals, Bapat has written books on linear algebra published by Hindustan Book Agency,<ref>{{cite web|title=Texts and Readings in Mathematics|url=http://www.hindbook.com/trims.php|publisher=Hindustan Book Agency}}</ref> Springer, and Cambridge University Press. He has served on the editorial boards of ''Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra'', ''Indian Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics'', ''Kerala Mathematical Association Bulletin'', and ''Linear and Multilinear Algebra''. He is national coordinator for the [[Mathematics Olympiad]] and was head of the [[Indian Statistical Institute]], Delhi Centre from 2007 to 2011.<ref name="bio" />

He is a [[Visiting Professor]] of Mathematics at [[Ashoka University]], India.

He held the position of President of [[Indian Mathematical Society]] from 2007 to 2008.<ref name="bio" />

==Fellowships and awards==
* J.C. Bose fellowship (2009)<ref name="bio" />
* Fellowship of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (2000).<ref>{{cite web | url = https://fellows.ias.ac.in/profile/v/FL2000001 | title = Prof. Ravindra Bhalchandra Bapat | author = Indian Academy of Sciences | access-date = 3 August 2023}}</ref>
